case_title: Sumitha Pradeep v. Arun Kumar C.K & Anr.
accused_occupation: Advocate (as alleged by the victim's counsel and recorded in the Special Judge's order; not a finding of this Court)
evidence_type: Victim's statement under s.164 CrPC; medical examination; counsellor's statement and educational report (as recorded in the lower court's order); no merits findings by this Court
aggravating_circumstances: Serious allegations; victim traumatised with adverse impact on academic pursuits; accused is a close relative of the victim
trial_court_outcome: No trial stated. Sessions Court (Special Judge) declined anticipatory bail by order dated 4 July 2022
high_court_outcome: High Court granted conditional anticipatory bail by order dated 25-7-2022
neutral_facts: The victim, a 12-year-old girl, is the niece of the accused, who is her maternal uncle. It is alleged that on 14 December 2021, while the victim was at the accused's house, the accused asked her to sit on his lap, hugged her, kissed her on the cheeks and tried to kiss her on the lips. It is further alleged that the accused attempted to disrobe the victim and made lewd comments. Before the incident the victim was an excellent student. Afterwards her academic performance fell markedly: her grades dropped from mostly top grades in the sixth standard to mostly lower grades in the seventh standard. Her parents took her for counselling. In the first counselling session she was continuously weeping and did not disclose the reason. In a second session she disclosed the incident. She had not told her mother earlier because of fear. A first information report was registered on 27 May 2022. A medical examination of the victim was conducted, and her statement under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was recorded. The complaint was made about six months after the alleged incident. The counsellor's statement and the victim's educational report were placed on the record to explain the delay.
physical_harm: No physical injury stated; victim traumatised with decline in academic performance
number_of_offences: 7 charged (IPC s.354A(1), s.354A(2), s.354A(3); POCSO ss.7, 8, 9, 11); 0 finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: FIR allegations and the victim's s.164 CrPC statement, referred to as supporting the prima facie case; no finding on merits
witness_credibility: Not assessed; Court expressly expressed no view on merits
bail_history: Sessions Court declined anticipatory bail (4 July 2022); High Court granted conditional anticipatory bail (25 July 2022); Supreme Court set aside the High Court order
trial_duration: offence: 14-12-2021; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 25-07-2022; Supreme Court: 21-10-2022
legal_representation: Appellant (victim's mother): Gaurav Agrawal, Ms. Anu K. Joy, Alim Anvar, Arvind Gupta. Respondents (accused and co-respondent): Raghenth Basant, Ms. Zehra Khan, Ajay Krishna, Harshad V. Hameed, Dileep Poolakkot, Mrs. Ashly Harshad. State counsel not separately identified
investigation_status: FIR registered (Crime No.442 of 2022, 27-5-2022); medical examination and s.164 statement done; investigation ongoing; counsel for accused stated a charge-sheet has been filed (not verified by Court)
procedural_irregularity: High Court's para 9 observations were unwarranted and made without regard to the binding Joy decision
appeal_history: Trial court: not applicable (no trial stated). Sessions Court: anticipatory bail declined (4 July 2022). High Court: conditional anticipatory bail granted (25 July 2022). Supreme Court: appeal by victim's mother allowed, High Court order set aside
prosecution_argument: Complainant (victim's mother) contended that the High Court wrongly granted anticipatory bail in a serious POCSO case and sought cancellation
defence_argument: Accused argued custodial interrogation was not required and that a charge-sheet had already been filed
legal_principle_applied: Prima facie case is the first consideration, followed by nature and severity of offence; absence of need for custodial interrogation alone is not a ground for anticipatory bail
precedent_relied_upon: Joy v. State of Kerala (2019) 1 KLT 935 (Kerala HC, on s.29 POCSO presumption in bail)
judicial_aggravating_factors: Serious nature of the allegations; victim's trauma and adverse academic impact
other_sentence_order: Investigating Officer granted liberty to proceed in accordance with law; High Court's conditional anticipatory bail set aside
